privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Wordleland is self-hosted for one private group. This says what it keeps about the people who use it, and why.
privacy.stored.heading: What is stored
privacy.stored.body: Your email address, for signing in and password resets. A Signal account identifier and your last-seen display name, if your results arrive from the group's Signal chat. Your Wordle results. If an admin corrects an entry, a record of what it said before.
privacy.why.heading: Why
privacy.why.body: To run the shared login, to match a Signal message to the right person, and to keep a trail of any correction an admin makes.
privacy.who.heading: Who can see it
privacy.who.body: Your own account details are visible only to you. Admins can see the group's roster and results to run the board. A read-only share link, if one exists for this installation, shows scores only — no email addresses or Signal identifiers.
privacy.cookies.heading: Cookies
privacy.cookies.body: Signing in, and remembering a theme or language choice, uses a few cookies. None of them are used for tracking, advertising, or shared with anyone outside this installation.
privacy.removal.heading: Leaving the group
privacy.removal.body: Leaving disables an account rather than deleting it, so past corrections keep their trail. Ask whoever runs this installation if you want your data handled differently.
